results.title: NSF Public Access Plan 2.0
results.content: Specific Online Digital Repositories Data management plans, or DMPs, are currently a required component of an NSF proposal.45 To ensure that funded researchers have considered data deposition and appropriate repositories, NSF plans to more explicitly and systematically require researchers to include, as part of these DMPs, details about how the data produced will be shared publicly and with other researchers and anticipated repositories for the data, and to ensure that costs associated with the chosen repository are reflected in the proposal budget request, as described in the PAPPG, per Section 3.D. To better align with other federal agencies, NSF will retitle such plans data management and sharing plans, or DMSPs. New requirements associated with the 2022 OSTP memo for making datasets publicly accessible will be conveyed to researchers via the standard NSF communication tools, such as the NSF Electronic Research Administrators Forum series, which NSF regularly hosts nationally with university research administrators.

results.title: Sharing Research Data in Collaborative Material Science ...
results.content: The objective of this paper was to examine the potential for the automated release of research data within the context of material science consortium projects, with adherence to the stipulated rules and contractual agreements, while also considering all relevant framework conditions, including those pertaining to protection and confidentiality. This was followed by the development of a methodological approach to the release of research data according to the needs of researcher in collaborative projects, such as automation of the release process, quality queries, reusability of data and more. research data management; collaborative research project; research data infrastructure; data release process; data sharing; data releasing. The authors propose a solution concept for the semi-automated process of releasing research data by combining state-of-the-art release methods with existing confidentiality agreements. The proposed concept is tailored to the specific requirements of material and engineering research projects and the anonymisation process of this concept is implemented in an open-source research data management tool to prove low-requirement realisability of this concept.
